topics.title: Introduction & Application of Service Costing
explain: Service costing, also known as operating costing, is used to determine the cost of rendering services rather than manufacturing physical goods.
It applies internally when a service cost centre provides support to internal responsibility centres (e.g., staff canteen, boiler house, internal IT support).
It applies externally when services are provided to outside customers as profit centres (e.g., passenger transport, hotels, banks, insurance).
All costs incurred during a specific period or volume are accumulated and expressed per unit of service.
topics.example: A company operating an in-house fleet of trucks for carrying raw materials to its factory uses internal service costing, while a commercial bus company uses external service costing.
remember: Service costing is also widely known as operating costing.
mistakes: Confusing internal support service cost centres with external profit-center services.

quiz.q: Service costing is also commonly known by which other name?
quiz.why: Service costing is also referred to as operating costing as it deals with operating a service.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of an internal service cost centre?
quiz.why: A staff canteen provides support services internally to staff within an organization.

topics.title: Service Costing vs Product Costing
explain: Tangibility: Services are intangible and cannot be stored, meaning there is zero finished goods inventory.
Cost Units: Service costing frequently utilizes composite cost units (such as passenger-km or room-days) to measure volume.
Material vs Employee Cost: Employee (labour) cost forms the major portion of service cost, unlike manufacturing where raw materials dominate.
Traceability of Costs: Indirect costs (like administration overheads) form a high proportion of total service cost, making direct tracing less economically feasible.

flow.title: Key Differences in Service vs Product Costing

topics.example: A software development firm has major employee salary costs and zero physical inventory, whereas a table manufacturing factory carries raw wood inventory and direct material costs.
remember: In service costing, employee cost usually exceeds material cost, and no inventory of services exists.
mistakes: Searching for closing stock of services in cost statements.

quiz.q: Why is there no inventory of output in service costing?
o: Services are intangible and cannot be stored
quiz.why: Services are intangible experiences rendered on demand and cannot be stored as physical inventory.

quiz.q: Which cost element typically dominates in service organizations compared to manufacturing?
quiz.why: Service industries rely heavily on human resources, making employee costs the primary cost driver.

topics.title: Service Cost Unit & Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
explain: A cost unit is the standard unit of quantity for which service cost is computed (e.g., kWh for electricity, patient-day for hospitals).
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are quantitative and qualitative metrics used to evaluate organizational performance against industry standards.
In Telecom, Average Return per User (ARPU) is a key revenue KPI.
In Transport and Logistics, KPIs include Truck Turnaround Rate, Lead Time (Order Cycle Time), and On-Time and In-Full (OTIF).

flow.title: Setting Cost Units and Measuring KPIs

topics.example: A hospital measures its cost per 'Patient Day' while tracking its 'Bed Occupancy Rate' as a primary KPI.
remember: Cost units express cost per unit of service, while KPIs measure operational efficiency and performance.
mistakes: Mixing up unit of cost (e.g., patient-day) with performance indicators (e.g., bed occupancy rate).

quiz.q: What is the standard cost unit typically used for Electricity Supply service?
quiz.why: Electricity supply cost is measured per unit generated/supplied, which is Kilowatt-hour (kWh).

quiz.q: In the transport and logistics sector, what does OTIF stand for?
quiz.why: OTIF measures the number of orders delivered according to the specified schedule and quantity.

topics.title: Composite Cost Unit & Equivalent Unit
explain: Composite Cost Unit combines two single measurement units into one (e.g., Tonne-km, Passenger-km, Patient-day).
Absolute Basis (Weighted Average): Summation of the individual products of weight/volume carried and distance travelled for each leg of a journey.
Commercial Basis (Simple Average): Product of total distance travelled and average load weight carried across all legs.

Equivalent Cost Unit: Used when a business offers different service grades (e.g., Standard, Deluxe, Luxurious rooms); all grades are converted into equivalent standard units using relative tariff ratios.

flow.title: Calculating Composite and Equivalent Units
steps: Calculate Absolute or Commercial Composite Units
Determine Weight/Tariff Ratios for Service Grades
Convert All Units into Equivalent Standard Units

topics.example: A lorry carrying 20 MT for 80 km and 12 MT for 120 km has an Absolute Tonne-km of (20×80) + (12×120) = 1,600 + 1,440 = 3,040 MT-km.
remember: Absolute Tonne-km sums each leg (Weight × Distance), while Commercial Tonne-km multiplies Total Distance by Average Load.
mistakes: Using simple average distance instead of weighted calculations for Absolute Tonne-km.

quiz.q: How is Absolute Tonne-Kilometer calculated?
o: Total distance multiplied by average load
Summation of (Weight carried × Distance) for each leg
Total distance divided by total load
Average load divided by number of trips
quiz.why: Absolute basis takes the actual sum of the products of weight carried and distance for each individual leg.

quiz.q: If a Deluxe room tariff is 2.5 times a Standard room, 1,000 Deluxe room-days equal how many equivalent Standard room-days?
quiz.why: 1,000 Deluxe room-days × 2.5 = 2,500 equivalent Standard room-days.

topics.title: Statement of Costs for Service Sectors
explain: Service cost statements collect costs over a specified period (month, quarter, year) and classify them by variability.
Fixed Costs (Standing Charges): Costs that remain constant regardless of distance or service volume (e.g., insurance, license fees, monthly driver salary).
Variable Costs (Running Costs): Costs directly linked to distance or activity volume (e.g., petrol, diesel, fuel usage).
Semi-Variable Costs (Maintenance Costs): Costs covering upkeep (e.g., repairs, tyres, spares).
Depreciation is treated as Fixed if time-based (efflux of time), but Variable if based on activity/usage level.

flow.title: Structure of Service Cost Statement
steps: Compute Total Operating Cost and Unit Cost

topics.example: A bus operator lists monthly garage rent under Standing Charges, diesel under Running Costs, and tyre repairs under Maintenance Costs.
remember: If information on semi-variable costs is missing, classify costs strictly into fixed and variable heads.
mistakes: Treating time-based depreciation as a variable running cost.

quiz.q: When is depreciation treated as a variable cost in service costing?
o: When calculated on activity level or usage
quiz.why: Depreciation based on activity or usage varies with service volume, making it a variable cost.

quiz.q: Under which head are garage rent and annual insurance premium classified for a bus operator?
quiz.why: Garage rent and annual insurance stay constant regardless of distance travelled, so they are Standing Charges.

topics.title: Costing of Transport Services
explain: Goods Transport cost unit is Tonne-Kilometer; Passenger Transport cost unit is Passenger-Kilometer.
Total Passenger-Km = Buses × Distance × Seating Capacity × Occupancy % × Days × Trips.
Standing Charges include monthly salaries of drivers/conductors, insurance, tax, garage rent, and time-based depreciation.
Running Costs cover fuel, lubricants, and activity-based wages; Maintenance Costs cover repairs, tyres, and spares.
Required Takings = Standing Charges + Running Costs + Maintenance Costs + Commission on Takings + Desired Profit.

flow.title: Transport Costing Procedure
steps: Add Commission and Desired Profit Margin

topics.example: A transport firm running 5 buses over 40 km carrying 30 passengers per trip calculates total passenger-kms to find the cost per passenger-km.
remember: Multiply one-way distance by 2 when calculating round trips.
mistakes: Forgetting to multiply by 2 for round trips (up and down) when calculating total kilometers.

quiz.q: What is the standard cost unit for a passenger transport company?
quiz.why: Passenger transport measures cost per passenger carried over one kilometer (Passenger-Kilometer).

quiz.q: If a bus makes 1 round trip per day between two towns 40 km apart, what is the total distance covered in 1 day?
quiz.why: 1 round trip = 2 single trips = 40 km × 2 = 80 km.

topics.title: Costing of Hotels and Lodges
explain: The standard cost unit for hotels is 'Guest Day' or 'Occupied Room Day'.
Tariffs vary by room category (Single, Double, Suite) and season (Peak season vs Off-season).
Equivalent room-days are calculated by applying room weightages (e.g., Double room = 2.5 times Single room).
Off-season concessional tariffs (e.g., 50% discount) reduce effective full-charge room-days.
Room Rent per day = Total Required Revenue (Costs + Targeted Profit) / Total Equivalent Full Room Days.

flow.title: Hotel Room Rent Ascertainment
steps: Compute Total Equivalent Single/Full Room Days
Sum Up Fixed, Variable & Rent Expenses
Divide Total Required Revenue by Equivalent Room Days

topics.example: A hotel with 100 rooms running at 80% occupancy for 180 peak days generates 14,400 occupied room days.
remember: Off-season room days at 50% tariff count as 0.5 equivalent full room days.
mistakes: Failing to adjust room days for occupancy rates or seasonal discounts.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a standard cost unit in the hotel industry?
quiz.why: Hotels measure costs and ascertain tariffs based on Occupied Room Days or Guest Days.

quiz.q: If an off-season tariff is 50% of peak tariff, 1,000 off-season room-days are equal to how many equivalent full-charge room days?
quiz.why: 1,000 off-season room days × 50% = 500 equivalent full-charge room days.

topics.title: Costing of Hospitals
explain: Hospital costing determines service costs across Out-Patient, In-Patient, Diagnostic (X-Ray/Scan), and Support departments.
Cost units: Out-Patient (per out-patient), In-Patient (per room day/patient day), Diagnostic (per test/case), Laundry (per 100 items).
Fixed Costs: Staff salaries, supervisor wages, building rent, depreciation, and administration.
Variable Costs: Patient food, medicines, laundry charges, extra bed hire fees, and doctor fees paid per patient.
Breakeven Point (in patient days) = Total Fixed Costs / Contribution per Patient Day.

flow.title: Hospital Financial & Cost Analysis
steps: Calculate Total Patient Days (Normal + Extra Beds)
Compute Total Revenue and Total Variable Costs
Deduct Fixed Costs to Find Net Profit

topics.example: A 35-bed CCU operating for 150 days yields 5,250 bed days; hiring extra beds at Rs. 100/day adds to variable cost.
remember: Breakeven patient days = Total Fixed Costs / Contribution per Patient Day.
mistakes: Including fixed supervisor salaries inside variable patient costs.

quiz.q: What is the formula for Breakeven Point in patient days for a hospital?
o: Total Fixed Costs / Contribution per Patient Day
quiz.why: Breakeven volume in patient days is calculated by dividing total fixed costs by contribution per patient day.

quiz.q: Which of the following is classified as a variable cost in a hospital's Critical Care Unit?
quiz.why: Medicines and food vary directly with the number of patient days, making them variable costs.

topics.title: Costing of IT & ITES Sector
explain: IT & ITES jobs are executed as unique 'Projects', which are heavily labour-intensive.
Direct manpower (Software Engineers, Project Leaders, Project Managers) costs are directly traceable to projects.
Support manpower (Quality Assurance, Testing, Staffing Managers) costs are treated as direct if dedicated, or apportioned overheads if shared.
Effort cost is measured per Person Day, Person Week, or Person Month.
Overhead absorption rate is usually computed as a percentage of Total Direct Salary.

flow.title: IT Project Cost Sheet Preparation
steps: Calculate Direct Salary Costs per Project
Apportion Common Support Overheads (% of Salary)

topics.example: A 6-month software project uses 3 engineers and 1 leader; overheads are absorbed at 50% of total salary cost.
remember: Total Effort Cost = Direct Manpower Salary + Apportioned Service Overheads + Dedicated Direct Expenses.
mistakes: Forgetting to absorb common overheads on direct salary costs when computing project cost.

quiz.q: In IT & ITES organizations, cost units for effort estimation are typically expressed as:
quiz.why: IT effort costs are calculated based on effort periodicity such as Person-Days, Person-Weeks, or Person-Months.

quiz.q: How are shared quality assurance staff costs treated if they cannot be traced to a single IT project?
quiz.why: If support manpower time is not traceable to a single project, it is treated as a service overhead and apportioned.

topics.title: Costing of Toll Roads
explain: Toll road projects involve Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) models where private developers design, build, operate, and transfer back the infrastructure.
Capital Costs include land acquisition, construction, materials, labour, pre-operative costs, and interest during construction.
Operating & Maintenance Costs include toll collection staff salary, routine repairs (potholes, cracks), electricity, and amortised depreciation.
Vehicle types are assigned weights (e.g., Two-wheeler = 1, Car/SUV = 4, Bus/LCV = 6, Heavy vehicle = 9) to convert traffic into equivalent vehicles.
Toll Rate per equivalent vehicle = (Daily Total Cost + Required Profit) / Total Daily Equivalent Vehicles.

flow.title: Toll Rate Calculation Flow
steps: Calculate Total Capital Cost & Concession Days
Determine Daily Amortised Cost & Operating Expenses
Convert Daily Traffic into Equivalent Vehicle Units
Divide Daily Target Revenue by Equivalent Units
Apply Vehicle Weights to Set Category Toll Fees

topics.example: If cost per day is Rs. 14,57,050 and total daily traffic equals 76,444 equivalent two-wheelers, base rate per unit is Rs. 19.06.
remember: Vehicle Type Toll Fee = Base Fee per Equivalent Unit × Assigned Vehicle Weight.
mistakes: Charging a uniform toll rate to all vehicles without applying vehicle weight ratios.

quiz.q: Under the BOT approach for toll roads, what does BOT stand for?
quiz.why: BOT stands for Build-Operate-Transfer, a private-public project partnership approach.

quiz.q: If the base toll rate per equivalent unit is Rs. 20 and Car/SUV weight is 4, what is the toll fee for a car?
quiz.why: Toll Fee for Car = Base Toll Rate (Rs. 20) × Weight Ratio (4) = Rs. 80.

topics.title: Costing of Educational Institutions
explain: Educational institutes receive One-time fees (admission, development), Recurring fees (tuition, lab, library), and Other incomes (hostel, canteen).
Operational costs include teaching staff salary, lab/computer maintenance, administration, and exam expenses.
Re-apportionment: Joint teaching costs (e.g., a teacher teaching both Arts and Commerce) are re-apportioned based on class counts.
Support costs are allocated on specific drivers: Lab attendants by practical lab classes; library staff by student library hours; peons/admin by student counts.
Fee per student to achieve targeted profit = (Cost per student per annum × (1 + Profit %)) / 12 months.

flow.title: Educational Stream Cost Allocation
steps: Re-apportion Shared Teacher Salaries by Class Ratios
Apportion General Admin & Exams by Students
Calculate Total Cost & Fee per Student

topics.example: A school calculates separate cost per student per annum for Arts, Commerce, and Science streams based on lab usage and teacher allocation.
remember: Peon and admin salaries are usually apportioned based on total student strength in each stream.
mistakes: Apportioning laboratory attendant salaries to Arts or Commerce streams that do not have lab classes.

quiz.q: How should library staff salaries in a school be apportioned among different streams?
o: Based on time spent at library by students of each stream
quiz.why: Library staff costs are apportioned according to the student-hours spent by each stream in the library.

quiz.q: If annual cost per student is Rs. 18,000 and the school targets 10% profit on cost, what is the required annual fee per student?

topics.title: Costing in Insurance Companies
explain: Income comprises policy premiums, re-insurance commissions, and fund management fees.
Expenditures are split into Direct (agent commission, claim settlement, legal fees) and Indirect (actuarial fees, marketing, admin).
Activity-Based Costing (ABC) is used to calculate policy profitability and customer profitability.
Activities are grouped into: (1) Pre-product development (market research, policy design) and (2) Post-product development (selling, policy issuance, claims management).
Cost per policy = Total Activity Cost / Number of policies sold; Cost per rupee of insured value = Total Cost / Total Insured Value.

flow.title: Insurance ABC Costing Steps
steps: Pool Overhead Costs into Activity Cost Pools
Group Costs into Marketing, Operations, IT & Support
Divide Total Cost by Number of Policies Sold
Calculate Cost per Rupee of Insured Value

topics.example: An insurer sold 528 policies with a total cost of Rs. 2,36,03,600; cost per policy is Rs. 44,703.79.
remember: Pre-product development happens before a policy is launched; post-product activities cover selling and claim processing.
mistakes: Including claim settlement costs under pre-product development activities.

quiz.q: Which of the following is considered a pre-product development activity in an insurance company?
quiz.why: Specifying coverage and terms occurs before the policy product is launched, making it a pre-product development activity.

quiz.q: If an insurance policy incurs total costs of Rs. 50,00,000 across 1,000 policies, what is the cost per policy?
quiz.why: Cost per policy = Total Cost (Rs. 50,00,000) / Number of policies (1,000) = Rs. 5,000.

topics.title: Costing in Financial Institutions
explain: Financial institutions (banks, NBFCs) use costing to evaluate product line and customer profitability.
Manpower cost (excluding interest and finance charges) is the largest operating cost element.
Direct professional labour (loan processors) is directly assigned to specific functions (e.g., home loan application processing).
Service overheads (chief officer salary, admin, telephone, depreciation) are apportioned to functions using appropriate driver percentages.
Cost per application = Total processing cost per month / Number of applications processed per month.

flow.title: Bank Loan Processing Costing Flow
steps: Divide by Applications Processed to Find Unit Cost

topics.example: A bank branch with Rs. 2,40,000 direct processor salaries and Rs. 45,250 apportioned overheads processes 500 home loan applications at Rs. 570.50 per application.
remember: Interest expense is treated separately from operational manpower and overhead costs in financial institution costing.
mistakes: Failing to apply the given percentage split for overheads shared across multiple bank functions.

quiz.q: In financial institutions, which operating cost component (excluding interest/finance charges) is usually the largest?
quiz.why: Manpower cost is the single largest operating cost element in financial service institutions.

quiz.q: If total monthly home loan processing cost is Rs. 2,85,250 for 500 applications, what is the cost per application?
quiz.why: Cost per application = Rs. 2,85,250 / 500 = Rs. 570.50.

topics.title: Costing for Power Houses
explain: Power house costing applies to electricity generation (thermal, solar, hydro) or steam generation.
Cost unit for electricity generation is Kilowatt-hour (kWh), commonly known as a 'Unit'.
Costs are categorized into Standing Charges (plant supervision, admin overheads, time-based depreciation) and Running Costs (operating labour, coal, oil, repairs, stores).
Coal cost is computed from coal consumption rate (e.g., 5 kWh generated per kg coal) and coal price per kg.
Effective units generated = Total units generated - Normal process loss - Internal auxiliary consumption + Emergency grid purchases.

flow.title: Power House Cost Statement & Rate Calculation
steps: Deduct Sales Recovery from Ash Disposal
Compute Cost per kWh (Total Cost / Net Units)

topics.example: Generating 20,00,000 kWh at a coal efficiency of 5 kWh/kg consuming coal @ Rs. 4.25/kg gives a coal cost of Rs. 17,00,000.
remember: Effective units available = Generated units - Normal loss - Internal consumption + Emergency purchased units.
mistakes: Forgetting to subtract internal departmental power usage when arriving at units available for sale or factory use.

quiz.q: What is the standard cost unit for electricity generation in power house costing?
quiz.why: The cost unit for electricity generation is Kilowatt-hour (kWh), commonly called a unit.

quiz.q: In power house costing, how are emergency grid purchase units treated when calculating effective units available?
quiz.why: Emergency grid purchases add to the total units available for use across operations.
